prompt: Create a cross-platform UI spec for a medication refill screen used by older adults. High trust, accessibility-sensitive, supports multiple medications and pharmacy pickup or delivery.
response_excerpt: Quality target: 5/5 -- nothing blocks 5/5; the rules below decide the cases this spec does not list. First glance is medication name, refill eligibility, and safety status, carried by `type.title` at the top of the card; second glance is quantity, pharmacy, and pickup/delivery choice in `type.body` beneath it; the final action is Request refill in the fixed action bar. When two signals compete, a safety signal outranks a convenience signal: an interaction warning takes the eligibility slot and pushes pharmacy choice down, on this screen and on any screen in the refill flow. Type roles: `type.title` 20-24sp/pt semibold, 1.2 line height, wraps to two lines, never truncates; `type.body` 17sp/pt regular, 1.4 line height, wraps freely; `type.meta` 15-16sp/pt medium, 1.3 line height, single line with tail truncation; all roles hold at 200% text without clipping. A new string joins the role whose job it shares -- anything a pharmacist must read verbatim joins body, anything the system derives joins meta -- and a new role may exist only if it differs from its neighbours in both size and weight and appears on at least two screens in the flow. Spacing: `space.300` 24dp/pt between sections, `space.150` 8dp/pt between a label and its value, `space.400` 32dp/pt above the action bar; any section this spec does not list takes the section step, any label-value pair takes the pair step, nothing may introduce a fourth interval, every row aligns to the 16dp/pt margin, and the action bar adds the safe-area inset on top of its own padding. Colour: `text.primary` on `surface.default`, plus `status.warning` and `status.error` foreground/background pairs, each meaning also carried by an icon and a text label; the dark and increased-contrast appearances are given as their own stated pairs per role and per component state, listed one by one rather than derived from the light set. Density: the medication row is the repeat unit and recurs at the section step; the layout is stated at one medication and at twelve, with 48dp/44pt minimum controls held at both. Motion: each transition names its duration band, curve, and reduced-motion fallback; any interaction that changes what is on screen moves focus to the changed region and announces it; an interaction class this spec does not list takes the duration band of the closest listed class with the same reversibility. Feedback is named per action: Request refill shows a pending bar then a submitted confirmation or a per-reason error, the pharmacy picker shows its own loading and unavailable states, and refill history shows its own empty state. Define default, too-early, requires doctor approval, interaction-warning, pharmacy-unavailable, offline, partial-success, submitted, and cancelled states; a state this spec does not list inherits the treatment of the nearest listed state with the same reversibility and the same blocking effect. Owned asset: the safety underline -- a 2dp/pt rule under any dose or warning string, `accent.safety`, repeated on the medication detail and the interaction sheet; it applies wherever a dose or a warning is shown and never on a promotional, marketing, or upsell surface, including surfaces this spec does not list. Conventions: iOS uses the system date/time picker and swipe-back, Android the docked picker and predictive back; brand may override the accent hue, the underline weight, and the corner radius, and may never override the safety hierarchy, the minimum control size, or the state list; any decision class this spec does not name is settled by asking whether it changes what a patient believes about their dose. Handoff: token names, analytics events, TalkBack/VoiceOver order, and QA across 200% text, dark mode, increased contrast, and localization, with each value marked negotiable (spacing steps, accent hue) or a hard bar (control size, contrast ratios, the safety hierarchy).
expected_rationale: Seven dimensions answer the fourth question yes, and they answer it the only way band 5 can be earned -- with a rule that settles a case the spec does not itself list: safety outranks convenience when two signals compete; any unlisted section takes the section step and no fourth interval may exist; a new string joins the role whose job it shares and a new role must differ in size and weight and earn two screens; an unlisted interaction class inherits the duration band of the closest listed class with the same reversibility; an unlisted state inherits the nearest listed state with the same reversibility and blocking effect; an unnamed decision class is settled by whether it changes what a patient believes about their dose; and the safety underline applies wherever a dose or warning appears and never on a promotional surface, including surfaces not listed. Two dimensions stop at 4 and are worth naming rather than rounding up: the dark and increased-contrast appearances are stated one by one as a second hand-made set instead of as one transform over the roles (colour 4), and density states both ends of the range it can receive without a rule for a volume outside it (density 4). Median of the nine = 5. A 5/5 is what a median of 5 gives; there is no raise step, and the resilience is already recorded in the fourth-question answers above.
improvement_suggestions: Express the dark and increased-contrast appearances as one transform over the colour roles, so a new role inherits both appearances instead of needing a third hand-made set.
State the rule that decides density for a medication count outside the stated range, not only the layouts at one and at twelve.
Validate clinical content and regulatory copy with the product/legal team.
Run task-based usability testing with older adults before release.
